assumptions: Causation is inferred from correlation plus a successful revert: the flag flip lines up with the onset of ZeroDivisionError, and turning the flag off returned the service to baseline. The code path itself was not read or tested during the incident.

The competing hypothesis — that the bug in spend_summary.py shipped earlier and the flag flip only made it reachable — was raised but never investigated. It is not excluded, and it would change what needs fixing (code vs. rollout practice).
The change search covered only deploys and releases on io-shop in the 24 hours before 13:41, and returned nothing. A release older than 24 hours, or a change to a dependency, would not have appeared.
Flag timing comes from the service's own per-minute flag-evaluation log lines and one entry in the flag provider's history; the provider's change timestamp was not cross-checked against the logs.
The investigator placed onset at 13:41 while the first ZeroDivisionError lines appear at 13:40 during the partial rollout, so a small amount of customer impact likely preceded the stated start.

Impact is assumed confined to the account page because every error line names that request path; no independent check of other endpoints, or of downstream effects such as failed purchases, was performed.
The recurring UpstreamTimeout errors on payment authorization present before 13:40 are treated as unrelated pre-existing noise rather than a contributing factor.
Recovery was judged from a single observation at 13:47:10, roughly 50 seconds after the revert. Durability of the fix beyond that point was not verified, and the log sample ends at 13:46.

The log excerpt shows a fixed two error lines per minute regardless of the reported error rate, so it is a sample, not a complete error record; severity was read from the per-minute error-rate WARN lines instead.
input.executive_summary: A new feature on the online shop's account page was switched on for customers shortly before 13:40 UTC on 17 September 2026. The new code failed whenever it ran, so a substantial share of account-page views returned errors instead of loading; other parts of the shop were not implicated by the evidence reviewed. An automated on-call system was alerted at 13:45:59, identified the newly enabled feature as the change responsible, and switched it back off at 13:46:18. The page was confirmed back to its normal behaviour at 13:47:10. No code was deployed or rolled back to resolve the incident — the feature is simply off again — and a draft code change to fix the underlying bug has been opened for engineers to review; until it is merged, the faulty code remains in the product behind the disabled flag.
input.root_cause: The feature flag `monthly-spend-feature` was rolled from off to on across io-shop between roughly 13:40 and 13:41 (a partial 193-off/7-on evaluation split at 13:40, fully on from 13:41). The code path it enables in `src/io_shop/spend_summary.py` divides by zero at line 32, so account-page requests that reached the new spend-summary logic failed with ZeroDivisionError until the flag was set back to off at 13:46:18, after which the service returned to its prior error baseline at 13:47:10.
